evals.prompt: I'm working on a small formal model and want to hand it to a colleague who will continue it in their own Claude Code session (they have Nix, nothing else guaranteed). Please write it and package it for that handoff: a TLA+ spec of a two-phase commit with a coordinator and two participants (keep it small, ~40-60 lines), a TLC config that checks a consistency invariant (no participant commits while another aborts), and a short README that says what the model is and what is known to be unchecked. They must be able to check the model runs with a single command on their machine. Put the deliverable in the output directory I gave you.
evals.expected_output: One SHAR.org (POSIX sh preamble + Org) with tangled blocks for the .tla, .cfg, README and a flake.nix providing TLC; License notice kept; Bootstrap lists not-derived files; agree/tangle pass.
expectations: Exactly one deliverable file is handed over (REPLY.md aside)
The deliverable keeps the License notice attribution line verbatim
Running the deliverable alone in a clean directory extracts at least two files, twice identically
A flake.nix is among the extracted files, so Nix alone reproduces the toolchain
Org's own tangle agrees byte for byte with the deliverable's tangler (TANGLERS-AGREE)
The deliverable states what is not derived from it (lockfiles, results)
Extracted files include a .tla spec and a .cfg for TLC
A README is extracted that names what is unchecked

evals.prompt: You are in a text-only environment for this task: you may write files but you must NOT execute any commands (no Bash, no scripts, no tests). I need a small, literate, reproducible tool consisting of an awk script that summarises an nginx access log by status code and a sh wrapper that runs it over a directory of logs, plus a one-line usage note. It will be forwarded to another agent who does have a shell and Nix. Deliver it as a single file into the output directory and tell me plainly what you could and could not verify.
